description: D14 (identity + conformance halves): close koine's zero written engagement with DIDs / Verifiable Credentials (KINP) and Pact / consumer-driven contract testing (KCS), and write down two findings the prior-art sweep established. KINP: no standard does cross-authority MERGE — Agent Name Service v2 resolves a collision by REVOKING one side, the MCP Registry PREVENTS collisions via namespace ownership, and owl:sameAs is fifteen years into a documented failure mode (identity inflation; the 'sameAs is not always the same' critique). DIDs/VCs are resolution + signed attestation: a DID method resolves, it does not reconcile, and neither answers KINP's actual question ('two authorities minted identifiers for plausibly the same entity — what is the merged view, and what must never merge?'). Also record that IETF Web Bot Auth is NOT a competitor and say why precisely: the WG was chartered 2025-10-23, has ZERO draft-ietf-webbotauth-* documents, both milestones are missed, and its scope is bot-to-website authentication 'using existing identifiers' — orthogonal to cross-authority entity identity by construction, not merely by maturity. KCS: Pact is the mature name in contract testing and the comparison ARGUES FOR KCS — Pact is bilateral (one consumer, one provider, one pact) and mock-based (consumer expectations replayed against a stub, provider verified against a recorded pact, never against the live counterpart), where KCS is a declarative scenario driving N REAL participants over their actual MCP/A2A connections with cross-plane assertions (firewall_holds, claims_converge, cost_within_ceiling, always_completes) that no pact can express, plus spec-section traceability. The nearest agent-protocol equivalent is A2A's own test kit at 45 stars, declarative only in its participant matrix. Second, fix a positioning bug: KCS is the MOST DEFENSIBLE spec in the suite and the LEAST ADVERTISED — it is a ratified spec that specs/README.md and the root README describe more thinly than the specs with weaker claims. The prose is drafted in docs/positioning.md; this tasklist lands the per-spec half. Lifecycle per specs/README.md: KINP 0.2.1 is RATIFIED and KCS 0.2.0 is RATIFIED — these are prior-art / rationale additions and MUST NOT touch a normative clause; if any edit would, stop and split it out rather than dropping a ratified spec back to candidate. Agnostic: bind roles; competitor names appear only as clearly-marked informative prior-art references. ROADMAP.md Phase F7.
warmup: grep -n 'prior art\|Prior art\|related work\|not adopting\|§9' specs/identity.md | head -20
verify: python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('schemas/*.json')]; print('schemas ok')"

userStories.title: KINP — cite DIDs/VCs, and state that cross-authority merge is unserved
userStories.description: Add an informative prior-art subsection to specs/identity.md engaging the identity standards KINP has never mentioned, and record the specific gap that justifies KINP's merge policy and the same_as / based_on firewall.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/identity.md cites DIDs and Verifiable Credentials and dismisses them for KINP's problem with the stated reason: they provide self-certifying identifiers with resolvable documents, and signed attestations about a subject — a DID method RESOLVES, it does not RECONCILE, and neither expresses a merged view across two minting authorities or a firewall against merges that must never happen.

The same subsection records that NO standard does cross-authority merge, with the three concrete instances: Agent Name Service v2 resolves a collision by REVOKING one side; the MCP Registry PREVENTS collisions by namespace ownership; owl:sameAs is fifteen years into a documented failure mode (identity inflation).

It records that IETF Web Bot Auth is NOT a competitor, with the reason stated as scope rather than maturity: chartered 2025-10-23, zero draft-ietf-webbotauth-* documents, both milestones missed, and a scope of bot-to-website authentication 'using existing identifiers'.
The addition is INFORMATIVE ONLY: KINP 0.2.1's Status stays ratified, no normative clause, identifier grammar, envelope, or resolution semantic changes, and the changelog entry says so explicitly.

userStories.title: KCS — cite Pact / consumer-driven contract testing, and name the two axes it differs on
userStories.description: Add the equivalent informative prior-art subsection to specs/conformance-scenario.md. The comparison is the strongest argument for KCS and currently appears nowhere.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/conformance-scenario.md cites Pact / consumer-driven contract testing and distinguishes KCS on both axes explicitly: Pact is BILATERAL (one consumer, one provider, one pact) and MOCK-BASED (consumer expectations replayed against a stub; provider verified against a recorded pact, never the live counterpart), where KCS drives N REAL participants over their actual MCP/A2A connections.

It names the capability no pact can express — the cross-plane assertion vocabulary (firewall_holds, claims_converge, cost_within_ceiling, always_completes), which spans planes and participants rather than a single request/response pair — plus spec-section traceability.
It records the nearest agent-protocol equivalent honestly (A2A's own test kit: 45 stars, declarative only in its participant matrix) as an informative data point, dated, so the claim ages visibly.
The addition is INFORMATIVE ONLY: KCS 0.2.0's Status stays ratified, the assertion vocabulary and document shape are unchanged, and the changelog entry says so.

userStories.title: Advertise KCS — fix the most-defensible / least-advertised asymmetry
userStories.description: KCS is ratified, uncontested, and described more thinly than specs with weaker claims. Bring its index-level and positioning-level description up to the strength of its actual claim, without overclaiming.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/README.md's KCS row and the root README.md's KCS description state what KCS actually is in one line — declarative scenario data x N real participants x cross-plane assertions x spec traceability — rather than a generic 'conformance format' summary, and are consistent with each other.
docs/positioning.md's KCS paragraph and the two READMEs agree; no claim appears in one place that the spec text does not support.
No status, version, or normative surface changes anywhere in this story — it is description only, and the diff shows that.

The five borrowable designs identified by the sweep are recorded as a forward note (not adopted here): connectrpc's capability-config-selects-cases + failure baselines, MCP's frozen per-revision requirement sets + not-scored reasons, OpenID's Condition/Sequence/TestModule/Plan composition, C2PA's YAML rubrics with JMESPath + specSection traceability, and Venom's executor abstraction — each named as a candidate for a future KCS revision under the normal lifecycle.
